name: security-php-stream-wrapper-input-review
intent: PHP stream-wrapper selection through lower-trust resource paths
artifacts: Runtime/wrapper configuration, file/resource callsites, path validation and resulting parser/include consumer.
trace: Trace untrusted scheme/path input into the actual enabled wrapper and operation, distinguishing read, write, include and network effects.
experiment: Use an isolated local fixture with inert files and a reviewed wrapper stub; compare intended local resource and one prohibited scheme.
disproof: A wrapper name or allow_url setting is not arbitrary execution; the reachable consumer and effective operation determine impact.
repair: Constrain resource schemes and final path authority at the consuming call, preserving intended file operations.
branch_decisions: Identify the enabled wrapper and the exact consuming function; file reading, include/require, network fetching and archive metadata have different behavior. Version and configuration change historical assumptions. A wrapper-looking string rejected by the actual consumer proves no side effect; model with an inert local stream and do not trigger remote or deserialization gadgets.
operational_method: Read the effective wrapper registry and the precise consumer function. Distinguish allow_url_fopen from allow_url_include and wrappers to which each applies; a local stream or include path is not equivalent to a remote fetch. For phar metadata inspect installed PHP behavior and any explicit metadata access rather than assuming all file operations deserialize it. Preserve the actual function/wrapper/configuration chain; a replacement inert wrapper demonstrates only its own semantics.
